title: agentarch evaluation result
description: The output of one evaluation run. This is the artifact that turns a declaration into evidence, and the reason conformance level L3 exists. A result may also declare that it has not been run: `status: not_run` with null values is an honest placeholder, and the schema requires the nulls rather than tolerating invented numbers.

status.description: `measured` means every value here came from a run that happened. `not_run` is a placeholder: the eval controls do not judge it, and conformance withholds L3 rather than failing the build. Declaring `measured` with fabricated values is the one thing this field exists to make impossible to do quietly.

completed_at.description: When the run finished, YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339. Freshness is checked against this. Null is required when status is not_run — a date on an unmeasured result is the same false claim in a smaller field.

subject.description: What was evaluated. A result whose subject differs from the agent as it stands today describes a system that no longer exists.

sha256.description: Null when the dataset does not exist yet. Never a made-up hash: a hash that matches nothing is indistinguishable from one that matches something until somebody tries to reproduce the run.

todo.description: What this dataset has to contain. Present on a placeholder, removed once it is real.

value.description: Null when not measured. The threshold beside it is not null, because deciding what you are committing to before you measure is the point.

deterministic_metrics.description: Names of the deterministic metrics in this run. Read by control.ai.eval.judge_not_sole_blocker: a judge is only allowed to block alongside one of these.

allOf.$comment: A measured result cannot carry nulls. Without this, `status: measured` next to `value: null` would validate, and the honest placeholder would become a way to claim evidence while providing none.
And the reverse: a placeholder must not carry numbers that look measured.
